question: Which of the five has been most explicit about serving mass-affluent clients, and what exactly have they said?

claims.text: Merrill is the most explicit, because it is the only one of the five that names a 'Mass Affluent' client segment as part of its 'Wealth Continuum'.
Merrill's investor-day presentation defines the mass-affluent segment as clients with $500K to $1MM in assets, listed alongside High Net Worth ($1MM-$10MM).
Merrill states it is 'Serving the wealth continuum of clients' across its Merrill and Private Bank businesses.
Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business provides a high-touch client experience through financial advisors focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets.
Merrill's Wealth Continuum defines the mass-affluent segment as $500K to $1MM in assets, while its advisory business is described as focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets.
Most recently, in 3Q26 Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, up 17%.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley names 'high and ultra-high net worth individuals' as its wealth client segment, not a mass-affluent segment; the only 'mass-affluent' mention is a third-party Cerulli Associates figure about 401(k) participants.
adjacent.differs_because: Morgan Stanley names 'high and ultra-high net worth individuals' (a higher wealth tier) as its wealth client segment, and the 'mass-affluent' mention is a third-party figure, not Morgan Stanley's own segment naming.
